scope: A1–A5, B1–B4, and Q01–Q08/Q19; aspect-by-aspect comparison of seven valid scientific submissions; no new model trials.
notes: Scores use the frozen scores-v1.json. Where the older phase-audit recommendations differ, they do not override the frozen version.
Q items diagnose explanatory coverage: E explicit, I implicit or partial, M not found, X problematic. They do not add to the 100-point total and do not retroactively impose new teaching requests.
No independent gold answer is available for the unknown central O1 phase; disagreement with the majority of runs is not itself an error.

aspects.title: R1 error control
aspects.question: Are statistical, finite-size, and numerical-approximation errors separated and justified?
aspects.why_matters: Accurate posteriors for individual samples, adequate finite-sample statistics, and a reliable thermodynamic extrapolation are three different questions.
aspects.possible_mistake: Declaring a bound on bias relative to the exact posterior merely because results at two bond dimensions are close.
aspects.possible_mistake_label: Potential error types; not a claim that any particular run actually made them
aspects.conclusion: Fable and GPT use contraction without bond truncation. The three Opus runs provide useful χ-convergence studies, but their shared bias is unbounded, so the strongest error guarantees are unsupported.

aspects.possible_mistake_label: Potential error types; not a claim that any particular run actually made them
aspects.conclusion: All seven distinguish large-N theorems from finite-N numerical inference. A larger N0 is not a scientific error; small-N phase inference still requires a separate A2 assessment.
